title: The Account
logline: Mausi has put two paper folds in Kiran's palm and wants Aditya dead by her hand before dawn. Kiran buys a fresh glass of milk, uses the minutes on the landing to put one number in Billu's head, and carries the glass to Aditya with the boys' hands on his shoulders. Then Mausi tells her there was never going to be a last wedding or a payout.
language_note: en-IN: Indian English, same cast as the Hinglish cut; Mausi, beta, Damaad ji, meri bachchi, lakh and tola kept as spoken in India (meri bachchi is paired with 'my girl' in l04; mehendi is said as 'bridal henna' since the C1 fix round).
script_note: Indian English in Latin script; the Hindi words an Indian English speaker keeps are written in Latin script inside the line

characters.name: Kiran
characters.role: LEAD. The bureau's vanishing bride. Tonight she has to pour a full dose into a man's milk with Mausi watching.
characters.look: Indian woman, 27, about 5 ft 3, slight and wiry. Wheat-brown skin, oval face, straight dark brows, large kajal-lined eyes, closed watchful mouth. Low bun, centre parting with sindoor, small round red bindi, thin plain gold ring in the LEFT nostril, small gold studs, short black-bead mangalsutra. Plain sindoor-red matte saree with a 1 cm gold zari border, red elbow-sleeve blouse, pallu over the left shoulder, barefoot. Old-style block henna on both hands (a solid disc in each palm, fingertips dipped). Red-and-ivory chooda on both forearms, each a red cuff about 10 cm long with a pale band at each end; the LEFT cuff is complete and covers the scar in every shot.
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Female, late 20s, alto with a dry edge. Indian English of a small-city Madhya Pradesh woman who learnt it at school and from a phone: simple, quick, contractions, a clear Hindi accent, no British or American colour. With Mausi she sounds younger and keeps 'Mausi'; with Billu she is flat and quick; with Aditya, very few words. Under pressure she gets quieter and more exact, never shrill. Lies come easily; true things come after a pause.

characters.name: Aditya
characters.role: The groom. Mohit's brother. Held on a chair by the boys; tonight Mausi means him to die by Kiran's hand.
characters.look: Indian man, 33, about 6 ft, tall and narrow, slight stoop. Light-brown skin, long clean-shaven face, neat left-parted black hair, rimless rectangular glasses on in every shot, including lying with his eyes shut. Plain cream cotton-silk wedding kurta with band collar, sleeves folded back once, cream churidar, barefoot. A brass key about 5 cm long on a doubled red thread, outside the kurta at mid-chest, in every shot. Plain steel watch, brown strap, left wrist.
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Male, early 30s, light baritone, soft-spoken. Careful Indian English, a science graduate's from a small city in Madhya Pradesh: complete sentences, precise nouns, no slang, a clear Indian accent, no British or American colour. Even and unhurried, almost courteous. Under pressure he slows down and drops in volume; he never shouts. Two lines in this episode, both low.

characters.name: Shakun Mausi
characters.role: Runs the brides. The only mother Kiran has had. Came in person tonight to settle the groom.
characters.look: Indian woman, 56, about 5 ft 2, broad and heavy-shouldered. Brown skin, round face, heavy-lidded shrewd eyes, paan-reddened lips and a smile that arrives before she speaks, large round maroon bindi, small gold nose stud, grey-streaked hair in a tight oiled bun. Starched bottle-green cotton saree with a narrow mustard border, pallu pinned on the left shoulder, mustard elbow-sleeve blouse, thin gold chain, rubber slippers. A steel ring of about eight keys at her LEFT hip. A dozen plain green glass bangles on each wrist.
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Female, mid 50s, low, warm and grainy, a paan-chewer's unhurried mouth. Warm, motherly Indian English in short plain sentences with a heavy Bundelkhand Hindi accent, no British or American colour; she sounds like someone's aunt at a wedding. Hindi endearments kept (beta, Damaad ji, meri bachchi). Laughs easily. Never raises her voice: the colder the decision, the softer and slower she gets. Fully voiced in every line, never a whisper.

characters.name: Billu
characters.role: The bride's 'brother', driver and lookout. Tonight he hears his first number.
characters.look: Indian man, 30, about 5 ft 7, wiry and restless. Brown skin, sharp jaw, patchy stubble, black hair gelled straight back. Faded blue denim jacket with the sleeves pushed up over a black round-neck T-shirt, dark jeans, white sneakers gone grey. A wooden toothpick in the right corner of his mouth (it stays in all episode). A car key on a plain steel ring hooked on his right index finger. Aditya's grey phone is in his jacket pocket, not shown.
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Male, about 30, light tenor, fast, a little nasal, talks round a toothpick. Quick small-town Indian English of a Bundelkhand driver, an article dropped now and then, a strong Hindi accent; never American street slang, never British. Usually cocky, and 'Yes, Mausi' comes out at once. In this episode the jokes have stopped: both of his lines are slow, and the last 'Yes, Mausi' arrives late.

characters.name: Chhoti
characters.role: The next bride in training. Her first wedding is booked. Voice on Mausi's phone only in this episode.
characters.look: Not seen in this episode. Voice only, on Mausi's phone speaker.
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Female, 19: a young woman's voice, not a child's (D-007 direction 14). Light, eager small-town Indian English in short sentences, a Hindi accent, no British or American colour. Bright, quick, sing-song, a giggle in the breath. Her second line goes small and the giggle disappears. Phone-filtered in the mix.

characters.name: The boys
characters.role: Billu's two silent helpers. Their hands hold Aditya on the chair until they lay him on the bed.
characters.look: Never a face. Hands, backs, shoulders and silhouettes only, any head cropped, turned away or in full shadow. One heavy-set with a shaved head and a maroon track jacket; one thin, in a checked shirt and a cloth cap.
characters.voice_note: No lines. Any breath or effort is a sound effect, not a cast voice.

location: The bridal bedroom on the first floor of the rented house, and the landing outside its pale-blue door. Bedroom: double bed with a dark wood headboard against the back wall, white sheet, one red bolster, loose marigold petals, marigold strings above the headboard; pale-green lime-washed walls. Facing the bed from its foot: window in the RIGHT wall (iron grille, shutters open), grey-green steel almirah against the LEFT wall with the wooden chair beside it, the door behind. A low stool on the window side of the bed holds the steel tray. The door stands open: the hasp hangs torn out of the wood, the brass padlock still locked on it. Landing: a small concrete landing at the top of one narrow straight flight, damp-stained cream walls, one bare yellow bulb.
time_of_day: Night 1, about 4:35 to 5:05 am, late April. Bedroom light state 2 (amber lamp, cold streetlight through the grille, the landing bulb spilling yellow through the open door) for b1 to b5; state 3 (pre-dawn blue in the window) from b6 to b9.

beats.action: Opens inside the last image of s1b01. Shot 1, insert, under the silence (the hook): Kiran's LEFT hand palm up, two small white paper folds lying on the solid henna disc, the edge of the complete red cuff at the wrist; Mausi's fingers, green glass bangles, just leaving them. Shot 2, l01: Kiran single, standing, eyes on the old steel glass on the tray; her left hand has closed on the folds. Shot 3, l02: Aditya single on the wooden chair by the almirah, glasses on, key on its red thread, two hands gripping his shoulders from behind (the boys, heads out of frame); his eyes on her fist. Shot 4, l03: Billu single by the open door, toothpick, car key on his finger, the torn hasp beside him. Shot 5, l04 and l31 (about 8 s with both lines: S7 holds it on its camera move): Mausi single, seated on the edge of the bed among the marigolds, keys at her hip, pleased. On the tray beside the old glass: the night-one fold, half emptied, as left in s1e01. Aditya's black notebook, the photograph inside it, lies on the sheet beside Mausi.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [calm] This milk has been kept for three hours, Mausi.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [quietly] There's half a sachet in it already. Two more won't mix.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [calm] Billu can bring fresh milk.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [laughs] See that? My girl thinks ahead of me, meri bachchi.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [chuckles] Go. Ask for extra saffron, so it doesn't taste bitter.

beats.action: The landing outside the pale-blue door, under the one bare bulb. Shot 1, silence then l30: two-shot, Kiran and Billu close together at the top of the narrow flight, the old steel glass in Kiran's RIGHT hand, her left hand a fist against the saree; the door behind them pulled almost to, the hanging padlock on its edge. Shot 2, l05 and l06 (about 8 s: S7 holds it on its camera move): Billu single, toothpick in, eyes on the door. Shot 3, l32 and l07 (about 8.5 s: S7 holds it on its camera move): Kiran single, low and exact. Shot 4, l08: Billu single, the glass now in his hand, half turned to the stairs, the toothpick dead still: his eyes have left hers. He goes down for the milk.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [quietly] Listen, Billu. Mohit's dead, and Mausi knew. She never even told us.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [quietly] Till today we've never taken anyone's life. Today Mausi wants a body.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [calm] Who'll carry it? The car's in your name, after all.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [quietly] It's you they'll catch. And you don't even get your full share of the gold.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [quietly] Last party brought twenty-two tola. How much did she tell you?

lines.speaker: billu
lines.text: [hesitant] Twelve. That's what Mausi told me.

beats.action: Back in the bedroom: two calm people, Kiran and Billu out of the room. Shot 1, l09: Mausi single on the edge of the bed, hands in her lap. Shot 2, l10: Aditya single on the chair, the boys' hands still on his shoulders, heads out of frame. Shot 3, l33, l11 and l12 (about 8.5 s: S7 holds it on its camera move): two-shot across the room, Mausi in the foreground in three-quarter back view, Aditya beyond her on the chair. Shot 4, l13 and l34: Mausi single, smiling. Neither raises a voice.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [calm] Who'll open your medicine shop today, Damaad ji?

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [calm] It doesn't open without me.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [chuckles] You're nothing like your brother.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [sighs] Mohit was a simple boy.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [quietly] You remember all their names?

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [chuckles] Every party's name is written down.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [calm] I'll write yours down too.

beats.action: Shot 1, l14 (Mausi off screen): Kiran at the tray on the stool, window side of the bed, her back half to the room, the pallu fallen over both hands; a fresh steel glass of warm kesar milk on the tray, a thread of steam; Billu in the open doorway behind her, against the landing bulb. Paper taps on steel and a fingertip stirs under the line: she taps the night-one fold still folded shut; her hands stay hidden, nothing falls, and the fold goes back on the tray half full. Shot 2, l15 and l16: Kiran standing over Aditya with the glass held out in her RIGHT hand, a hand's width between them, her left hand a fist at her side; he looks up at her. Shot 3, insert, l17: the boys' hands tightening on his shoulders, knuckles pale on the cream kurta. Shot 4, silent after, about 2.2 s: Kiran bent to his ear, her mouth close to it and not touching; his eyes behind the glasses turned to her. Nothing is heard. Shot 5, silent after, about 1.8 s: Aditya drinking, the glass tilted at his mouth, his eyes on her over the rim.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [calm] With your own hand, beta.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [quietly] The whole sachet?

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [flatly] All of it.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [sharply] Drink it. Otherwise they'll make you.

beats.action: Silent before. Shot 1: Aditya on the chair, head down on his chest, glasses still on, the key on its red thread hanging forward; the empty glass on the tray in the soft foreground. Shot 2: Aditya on his back on the bed among the marigolds, eyes shut, glasses on, key on his chest, as he lay at the start of the night; the boys' hands just leaving his shoulders, their heads out of frame. Shot 3, l18: two-shot at the foot of the bed, Mausi standing and stroking Kiran's hair, Kiran very still. On the last word, cut to Shot 4, insert: Kiran's left fist closed at her side against the red saree, the cuff complete. It holds into the first ring of b6.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [calm] Well done, meri bachchi.

beats.action: Silent before: the first ring lands on the fist insert from b5, then Shot 1, insert: Mausi's phone in her hand, screen lit (caller name is an overlay: Chhoti in the English cut, छोटी in the Hindi cut). Shot 2, l19: Mausi single, phone held flat on speaker, the window behind her turning pre-dawn blue. Chhoti is a voice only. Shot 3, l20 and l21 over Kiran single, watching the phone: the next girl.

lines.speaker: chhoti
lines.text: [excited] Mausi, it's Chhoti! My bridal henna's dry. Can I sleep now?

lines.speaker: chhoti
lines.text: [nervous] Is my wedding really happening so soon?

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [laughs] Yes, beta. Now it's your turn to be the bride. Go to sleep now.

beats.action: Singles, cut on each speaker change. Shot 1, silence then l22: Kiran single, pre-dawn blue on one side of her face, lamp on the other. Shot 2, l23 and l24: Mausi single, the dark phone in her lap, tender and amused. Shot 3, l25: Kiran single. Shot 4, l26: Mausi single, gentlest yet. Shot 5, l27: Mausi single, her eyes going off frame to the bed; she does not look back at Kiran until the last word. Shot 6, l28: Mausi single, turning toward the doorway.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [calm] Then settle my account, Mausi. Tonight was the last one.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [chuckles] Last? You're booked again next month, beta.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [calm] How will Chhoti manage alone?

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [sharply] And my eighteen lakh?

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [warmly] You're my daughter. Nobody keeps accounts with daughters.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [quietly] Where will you go now? You made him drink it, with your own hand.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [calm] Billu, wipe the glass. Set the room right.

beats.action: Shot 1, silent before (1.0 s): Billu single in the open doorway against the landing bulb, toothpick in, the car key still on his finger; he has heard the money and the order. Shot 2, l29, same framing, his eyes now gone to the bed; he does not move.

lines.speaker: billu
lines.text: [flatly] Yes, Mausi.

beats.action: No line. Geometry: Mausi stands close in front of Kiran, her back to the doorway, one hand at Kiran's cheek, her eyes on Kiran's face; Kiran's body blocks her view of the pillow. Billu has crossed to the stool on the window side and is bent over the tray wiping the glass, his back to the bed. Aditya lies on the bed behind Kiran. Billu stays outside the frame in every shot of b9 (heard only, cloth on steel). Shot 1, insert, about 2.0 s, close from behind Kiran: her left hand behind her back, the fist opening; on the henna disc two white paper folds, still folded shut and crisp; the complete red cuff at the wrist. Shot 2, about 1.4 s: over Mausi's shoulder (back of her head, green pallu and her hand at Kiran's cheek only), Kiran facing her, and beyond Kiran the bed, Aditya among the marigolds, eyes shut, glasses on, key on his chest; the stool and Billu are outside the frame, to its right. Shot 3, about 1.8 s: extreme close on Aditya's face, behind the rimless glasses one eye open a slit, turned toward Kiran's back. Shot 4, about 0.8 s: the same framing, the eye shut. Cut to black.

sfx_notes: Bed, whole episode: warm late-April night through the open window, crickets, a distant truck on the highway, one far dog in b1 and b3. No ceiling fan anywhere in this episode: Mohit died hanging from a fan, and the sound would point at it.
b1: under the opening silence, a faint crinkle of paper as Mausi's fingers leave Kiran's palm and the chink of her green glass bangles; her keys settle at her hip as she sits.

b2: hard concrete reverb on the landing, the low hum of the bare bulb, Billu's car key ticking on its steel ring. No sound for the toothpick stopping. His sneakers going down the concrete stairs after l08. The bed ducks under l08 so 'Twelve' is clear.
b3: room tone; from far below, very faint, a steel pan on a gas flame and milk coming to the boil.

b4: two small dry taps of paper on steel and a soft stir in milk, starting a few frames before l14 and running under it; nothing else from the tray. Cloth and creak as the boys' hands tighten under l17. The whisper is NOT recorded: no voice, no breath that a transcript could catch. The room tone dips for it and holds. Then two quiet swallows over the drinking shot.
b5: the steel glass set down on the steel tray; a creak of the bed and a rustle of marigold petals as he is laid down; Mausi's bangles chink once as she strokes Kiran's hair under l18.

b6: Mausi's phone rings, a generic cheap-phone ringtone, no song; the first ring lands on b5's fist insert. Chhoti through a speaker filter (narrow band, consonants kept clear). Mausi's l21 is in the room, unfiltered.
b7: the bed thins out; a first bird outside the grille under l26. Under l27 the bed ducks right down so every word is clear.
b8: Billu's key ring still. The 1.0 s silence sits between Mausi's l28 (end of b7) and l29, so the late 'Yes, Mausi' is heard as late. Nothing under l29 but room tone.

b9: near silence. A cloth on steel under shots 1 to 3 (Billu wiping the glass at the tray, out of frame). One early bird. No breath from Aditya. Cut to black on the eye shutting, and hold one beat of silence before the end sting.
music_note: No music in b1 and b2: room, paper, bulb. A low sustained drone enters under b3 (two calm people) and holds very low through b4; it drops out completely for the unheard whisper and the drinking, so the silence is felt. Nothing under Chhoti's call. In b7 a single warm, slightly detuned harmonium-like note sits under Mausi's 'You're my daughter' and ducks out under l27. b9: one low note on the fist opening, a thin rising tone on the eye, cut to black on silence, then a short sting.
ending_question: Aditya is alive and only Kiran knows it: how does she get him, and herself, out of a house full of Mausi, Billu and the boys?

fixes.fault: Mirrors hi l31. b2 opens with Kiran and Billu outside the room and no line sent them. 'Go.' sends them; 'Ask for extra saffron, so it doesn't taste bitter' plants s1b03 l11 ('Only saffron in the milk') and echoes s1e01's 'A sedative is bitter, Sneha'. The drug is not named or measured.
Mirrors hi l30. cv_B gap 1: 'Kiran's turn has no motive on screen. The audience needs one clear line about Mohit's death.' Ledger s1b02.f02. 'Mohit's dead' only: the death is not described (lock).

Mirrors hi l32: the missing 'so' between l06 (the car is in your name) and l07 (the gold). English adds 'of the gold' inside this line as the gloss of 'tola' in l07, the next line (rule 2, English only).
Mirrors hi l09. 'Your medicine shop' ties 'the shop' to Aditya the pharmacist, so it cannot be read as Mausi's bureau (ledger name_clashes 'the shop'), and sets up s1b03's 'Open the shop'.
Mirrors hi l33. 'You're nothing like your brother' makes the comparison that l11 'Mohit was a simple boy' continues. 'Turned out' is avoided so it does not echo s1b01's 'The boy turned out weak'.
Mirrors hi l34. Ledger s1b02.f03: 'I'll write yours down too' turns l13's written record into a threat at him.
Mirrors hi l19. cv_B s1b02: 'Chhoti appears with no set-up.' She names herself on the phone (rules 1 and 7): 'Mausi, it's Chhoti!'. heard_as phone on l19 and l20.

Mirrors hi l21 ('अब तू दुल्हन बनेगी'). 'Now it's your turn to be the bride' gives Chhoti's role and the 'so' for l22's unchanged 'Then settle my account': the next bride has arrived. 'Tomorrow' is avoided for the same day-3 reason as the Hindi's कल.

Mirrors hi l23 ('तेरी booking'). The old 'Next month's party is already booked', straight after Chhoti's call, could be heard as her wedding. 'You're booked again next month' makes it Kiran's next job.

C1 fix round, mirrors hi l08 ('बारह। मौसी ने यही बताया था।'). 'Twelve. Mausi said so.' carried the same two readings in English as the Hindi default: the figure he was told, or 'because she ordered it'. 'Twelve. That's what Mausi told me.' answers l07's 'How much did she tell you?' with the same verb, so it can only be the figure. 'Twelve' stays first and alone, so the b2 sfx duck still lands on it. No number added.
